topology: PC1 reaches the independent AUTH1 TACACS+ LAN through R1. Passwords authenticate locally on R1; only permission decisions go to AUTH1. The server lab passwords deliberately differ from local passwords.
implemented: Third ENCOR Security lab and35 total ENCOR entries with accurate catalog counts, current-host permalinks, practice and completed reference. Existing CCNA AAA labs and both earlier ENCOR Security labs remain available.

Authentication-only admin SSH starts at user EXEC; explicitly binding named VTY-EXEC enables TACACS+ shell permissions and privilege15/admin versus privilege1/operator. Server authentication and accounting counters stay zero in the permission workflow.
A server Deny shell response closes SSH after successful local authentication; a local privilege15 credential cannot override the explicit rejection.
Level15 VTY-CMDS checks apply before privileged EXEC and configuration commands. A real authorized SSH session creates Loopback10 and delivered PC1 echo replies prove the resulting interface works.

Lowering the remote admin privilege blocks configure terminal in an already privileged session, without replacing the live session identity. A separate denial inside Loopback10 configuration leaves its existing description unchanged.

Service-only outage produces actual TCP49 communication errors then local EXEC/command authorization. Server pings remain available; powering off or disconnecting the server cannot substitute for this exercise.

Local command fallback creates a real temporary Loopback20, requiring delivered echo replies. An operator elevated with enable is still denied by local command authorization because its username privilege remains1.
Named local CONSOLE recovery works during the outage without remote EXEC or command authorization. Restoration requires new healthy remote EXEC and command decisions plus clean remote logout.

Final live checks require matching restored server policy, TAC-GROUP then local list order, local authentication, all sixteen SSH-only VTYs and five-minute timeout, configuration-command authorization, saved R1 configuration, correct Loopback10 and removed temporary Loopback20.

Credential-free runtime authorization observations copy configured methods, actual method outcomes, service/interface/key-match state, requested kind, session identity and redacted command. TCP transaction IDs and server-side accepted/rejected authorization requests corroborate observations. Existing decisions and enforcement are preserved.

Practice starts0/20; completed reference has seven live goals and no pre-earned permission incidents or traffic. Portable saves retain earned observations but clear runtime, sessions, packet traces and receiver logs. Imported criteria reject unknown checks and foreign/missing roots.
Diagnostic test aaa authentication traffic, generic log text, none/if-authenticated shortcuts and disabled configuration-command enforcement cannot replace the required authorization evidence.
scope: IOS EXEC and privilege-based level15 command authorization using TACACS+ with local fallback. Arbitrary TACACS+ per-command/argument regex rules and external wire interoperability are not implemented or claimed.
RADIUS EXEC attributes are covered by the existing RADIUS AAA Client lab. This exercise does not configure RADIUS command authorization, new accounting services or packet formats.
Primary Cisco authorization documentation reviewed. No new live CML capture was performed; existing IOS/NX-OS CML AAA contracts are covered by full native regression.

The normal server AAA form controls service availability, IOS privilege and Allow/Deny shell. Its existing accounting panel remains empty in this lab; client show commands expose real authorization counters.
No terminal styling, UI theme/layout, node artwork or dependency changes.

references.title: Cisco IOS XE17.14 Catalyst9300: Configuring Authorization
